# G3W-SUITE Documentation

## Access policy examples

This table summarizes permissions by role.

[Read online](/en/docs/access-policy-examples/)

# Access policy examples

## Summary table of access/administration policies
This table summarizes permissions by role.

| Role | Admin1 | Admin2 | Editor1 | Editor2 | Viewer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Description** | Advanced administrator with access to Django administration. | Basic administrator. | Macro-group manager. | Group manager. | Viewer. |
| **Users** | Manages Editor1, Editor2 and Viewer users. | Manages Editor1, Editor2 and Viewer users. | Manages Editor2 and Viewer users. Other Editor1 users cannot manage the users this Editor1 creates. | — | — |
| **Cartographic macro-groups** | Creates and manages macro-groups and assigns them to Editor1 users. | Creates and manages macro-groups and assigns them to Editor1 users. | Manages content in assigned macro-groups. | — | Views macro-groups in the front end according to their credentials. |
| **Cartographic groups** | Creates and manages groups and sets their access and management permissions. | Creates and manages groups and sets their access and management permissions. | Creates and manages groups within assigned macro-groups. | Manages assigned groups. | Views groups in the front end according to their credentials. |
| **WebGIS services** | Publishes and manages services and sets their access and management permissions. | Publishes and manages services and sets their access and management permissions. | Publishes and manages services within the groups they manage. | Publishes and manages services within assigned groups. | Views services according to their credentials. |
| **Editing** | Can edit all layers with editing enabled. | Can edit all layers with editing enabled. | Can edit layers with editing enabled in the projects they manage. | Can edit layers with editing enabled in assigned groups. | Can edit layers with editing enabled if their credentials allow it. |

## Examples of organization

### Basic organization
In this case the main administrator (**Admin role**) manages users, containers and all WebGis services
Access to Cartographic Groups and individual WebGis services can be limited to system users (**Viewer** role) or to free access (**Anonymous user**)

**Contents organized on a single level (Cartographic groups)**

```mermaid Basic organization on one level: Admin manages cartographic groups directly, and viewers can access authorized WebGIS services
flowchart TB
  admin["Admin"] --> groups["Cartographic groups"]
  groups --> a1["Service A"] & a2["Service B"] & a3["Service C"] & b1["Service A"] & b2["Service B"] & b3["Service C"]
  a2 --> a2w1["WebGIS 1<br/>Viewer"] & a2w2["WebGIS 2<br/>Viewer"] & a2w3["WebGIS 3<br/>Viewer"]
  a3 --> a3w1["WebGIS 1<br/>Viewer"] & a3w2["WebGIS 2<br/>Viewer"]
  b2 --> b2w1["WebGIS 1<br/>Viewer"] & b2w2["WebGIS 2<br/>Viewer"] & b2w3["WebGIS 3<br/>Viewer"]
```

**Contents organized on two levels (Cartographic macro-groups and cartographic groups)**

```mermaid Basic organization on two levels: Admin manages both macro-groups and their cartographic groups, and viewers can access authorized WebGIS services
flowchart TB
  admin["Admin"] --> a["Macro-group: Administration A"] & b["Macro-group: Administration B"]
  a --> a1["Service A"] & a2["Service B"] & a3["Service C"]
  b --> b1["Service A"] & b2["Service B"] & b3["Service C"]
  a2 --> a2w1["WebGIS 1<br/>Viewer"] & a2w2["WebGIS 2<br/>Viewer"] & a2w3["WebGIS 3<br/>Viewer"]
  a3 --> a3w1["WebGIS 1<br/>Viewer"] & a3w2["WebGIS 2<br/>Viewer"]
  b2 --> b2w1["WebGIS 1<br/>Viewer"] & b2w2["WebGIS 2<br/>Viewer"] & b2w3["WebGIS 3<br/>Viewer"]
```

### Medium organization
In this case the main administrator (**Admin role**) wants to delegate some secondary administrators (**Editor2** role) in managing the contents (WebGis) of the individual Cartographic Groups.

User management will remain limited to the main administrator (**Admin** role)

Access to Cartographic Groups and individual WebGis services can be limited to system users (**Viewer** role) or to free access (**Anonymous user**)

**Contents organized on a single level (Cartographic groups)**

```mermaid Intermediate organization on one level: Admin delegates content management for cartographic groups to Editor2, and viewers can access authorized WebGIS services
flowchart TB
  admin["Admin"] --> groups["Cartographic groups<br/>Editor2"]
  groups --> a1["Service A"] & a2["Service B"] & a3["Service C"] & b1["Service A"] & b2["Service B"] & b3["Service C"]
  a2 --> a2w1["WebGIS 1<br/>Viewer"] & a2w2["WebGIS 2<br/>Viewer"] & a2w3["WebGIS 3<br/>Viewer"]
  a3 --> a3w1["WebGIS 1<br/>Viewer"] & a3w2["WebGIS 2<br/>Viewer"]
  b2 --> b2w1["WebGIS 1<br/>Viewer"] & b2w2["WebGIS 2<br/>Viewer"] & b2w3["WebGIS 3<br/>Viewer"]
```

**Contents organized on two levels (Cartographic macro-groups and cartographic groups)**

```mermaid Intermediate organization on two levels: Admin manages both macro-groups, Editor2 manages cartographic group content, and viewers can access authorized WebGIS services
flowchart TB
  admin["Admin"] --> a["Macro-group: Administration A"] & b["Macro-group: Administration B"]
  a --> a1["Service A<br/>Editor2"] & a2["Service B<br/>Editor2"] & a3["Service C<br/>Editor2"]
  b --> b1["Service A<br/>Editor2"] & b2["Service B<br/>Editor2"] & b3["Service C<br/>Editor2"]
  a2 --> a2w1["WebGIS 1<br/>Viewer"] & a2w2["WebGIS 2<br/>Viewer"] & a2w3["WebGIS 3<br/>Viewer"]
  a3 --> a3w1["WebGIS 1<br/>Viewer"] & a3w2["WebGIS 2<br/>Viewer"]
  b2 --> b2w1["WebGIS 1<br/>Viewer"] & b2w2["WebGIS 2<br/>Viewer"] & b2w3["WebGIS 3<br/>Viewer"]
```

### Advanced organization
In this example, the **Admin** assigns an **Editor1** to each cartographic macro-group to delegate content management.

**Editor1** users can in turn delegate some secondary administrators (**Editor2** role) in managing the contents of the individual Cartographic Groups.

**Editor1** users can manage accounts delegated to them. Account permissions and macro-group assignments are separate; macro-groups do not provide tenant isolation.

Access to Cartographic Groups and individual WebGIS services can be limited to system users (**Viewer** role) or to free access (**Anonymous user**).

In this case, usually, the main administrator (**Admin** role) only takes care of creating the Macrogroups, the **Editor1** users and associating them correctly

```mermaid Advanced organization: Admin assigns an Editor1 to each independent macro-group; each Editor1 manages its own users and can delegate group content to Editor2
flowchart TB
  admin["Admin"] --> a["Macro-group: Administration A<br/>Editor1"] & b["Macro-group: Administration B<br/>Editor1"]
  a --> a1["Service A<br/>Editor2"] & a2["Service B<br/>Editor2"] & a3["Service C<br/>Editor2"]
  b --> b1["Service A<br/>Editor2"] & b2["Service B<br/>Editor2"] & b3["Service C<br/>Editor2"]
  a2 --> a2w1["WebGIS 1<br/>Viewer"] & a2w2["WebGIS 2<br/>Viewer"] & a2w3["WebGIS 3<br/>Viewer"]
  a3 --> a3w1["WebGIS 1<br/>Viewer"] & a3w2["WebGIS 2<br/>Viewer"]
  b2 --> b2w1["WebGIS 1<br/>Viewer"] & b2w2["WebGIS 2<br/>Viewer"] & b2w3["WebGIS 3<br/>Viewer"]
```
## Access portal

This section describes the different sections of the access portal and how to login to the Administration Panel

[Read online](/en/docs/access-portal/)

# Access portal
_**This section describes the different sections of the access portal and how to login to the Administration Panel**_

## The login portal sessions
The G3W-SUITE application is accessible via any internet browser (FireFox and Chrome recommended) via the URL address defined during installation

The [optional front-end portal](https://github.com/g3w-suite/g3w-admin-portal) provides the pages shown below. In a default installation without the portal, the site root opens the administration dashboard and redirects visitors who are not signed in to the login page. With the portal enabled, the dashboard is under `/admin/`.

The home page will contain, in addition to a brief and customizable presentation of the service, also:

 * a **menu at the top right side** ![Screenshot: G3W-SUITE Portal Menu Toprigth](/img/manual-english-g3wsuite-portal-menu-toprigth.avif) with the following items:
   * **`Change language`**
   * **`Go back to the home page`**
   * **`Login`**
 * a **panel menu on the right** with the following items:
   * **`Maps`**
   * **`Info`**


![Screenshot: G3W-SUITE Portal Frontend](/img/manual-english-g3wsuite-portal-frontend.avif)

Most of the information shown in the access portal can be defined from the **`Configurations -> Edit General Data` session**, accessible from the icon located in the upper right corner of the Administration Panel.

![Icon: G3wclient Config](/img/manual-english-g3wclient-icon-config.avif)

### Info
The **Info** session can contains a small introduction and contact information for your company or public facility.

![Screenshot: G3W-SUITE Portal Aboutit](/img/manual-english-g3wsuite-portal-aboutit.avif)

### Maps
Organize WebGIS services in **Cartographic Macrogroups and Cartographic Groups**.

By accessing the **Maps** session, the **Macrogroups** (if present) will be displayed, access to the Macrogroup will allow you to view the associated **Cartographic Groups** and from these access the list of individual **WebGis services**.

The MacroGroups, Groups and WebGis services listed will be those defined as free access.

If you have a user for access, you can authenticate yourself through the **Login session**.

Following authentication, the **Maps** page will also show the MacroGroups, Groups and WebGis services with restricted access and on which the user has access permissions.

![Screenshot: G3W-SUITE Portal Macrogroups](/img/manual-english-g3wsuite-portal-macrogroups.avif)

![Screenshot: G3W-SUITE Portal Groups](/img/manual-english-g3wsuite-portal-groups.avif)

### Login
If you have a user with login credentials, you can authenticate yourself through this session by entering your user and password.

If you are an **Administrator** or **Editor** of 1 or 2 level, you can also access the Administration session.

Once logged in, you access the **Admin** session and from here, via the **"Backend"** button to the Administration panel

![Screenshot: G3W-SUITE Portal Login](/img/manual-english-g3wsuite-portal-login.avif)

## Description of the interface

Use the Administration Panel to publish QGIS projects and configure their WebGIS services.

The main page of the Administration Panel shows the following items, depending on your permissions and the installed modules:
 * **`a bar at the top`:**
   * **Frontend:** to return to the landing page when the optional portal is enabled
   * **Username:** to edit your profile and log out
   * **Language:** to choose the interface language
   * **A gear icon** ![Icon: Configuration](/img/manual-english-iconconfiguration.avif): to access a menu with:

       **-->  Sistem Information**: information on operating system versions, QGIS Server, DB management, geographic libraries and anything else related to the suite

       **-->  Edit general data**: to set information shown in the front-end portal

       **-->  Django Administration** (only for Staff user): to configure/managme Django advanced settings

       **-->  Files:** to access the File Manager tool

       **-->  Images:** to define the main images of the FrontEnd home page

 * **`a text menu on the left`:**
   * **Dashboard:** Administration dashboard
   * **Cartographic Groups:** to create/manage cartographic groups
   * **Macro Cartographic Groups:** to create/manage Cartographic MacroGroups
   * **Users:** to create/manage single users and/or user groups
   * **List of active modules:** to activate/manage the functional modules active in your installation
 * **`a dashboard in the center of the page`**
   * **Dashboard:** to access to list of Cartographic Groups
   * **Module list:** to access the respective settings

![Screenshot: G3W-SUITE Administration Desk](/img/manual-english-g3wsuite-administration-desk.avif)

## Front end portal customization
If the [optional portal](access-portal.md) is enabled, use the **Administration Panel** to customize its content.

Open the **Configurations** menu ![Icon: Configuration](/img/manual-english-iconconfiguration.avif) at the top right and choose **Edit general data**.

![Screenshot: G3W-SUITE Administration Configuration](/img/manual-english-g3wsuite-administration-configuration.avif)

In the **`General suite data`** form you can define all the informations that will appear on the portal home page
 * **`Home data`:** info that will appear on the front end landing page
 * **`About data`:** info that will appear in the **About it** session
 * **`Group map data`:** info that will appear in the **Maps** session
 * **`Login data`:** info that will appear in the **Login/Administration** session
 * **`Social media data`:** links to the social channels that will appear in the **About it** it session
 * **`Map Client data`:** main title to be displayed in the cartographic client bar

## Bottom panel and time series

The bottom part of the left bar contains the following items:

[Read online](/en/docs/bottom-panel-and-time-series/)

# Bottom panel and time series

## Bottom session

The bottom part of the left bar contains the following items:

### Add layer

Through this tool the user can add custom WMS, TMS or local file layers to the WebGIS service.

#### WMS (URL)

The user can add one or more WMS service by defining:
 * **WMS URL**
 * **Name**

Clicking on Connect buttom, you can view the list of layers associated with the service and choose which one (or which ones) to load into the map by defining:
 * the **Projection system** to be associated
 * the **Position** (top or buttom) with respect to the other layers of the project
 * the **Opacity** of the layer
 * an alternatice **Name** respect the original
 
![Screenshot: G3wclient Add WMS](/img/manual-english-g3wclient-add-wms.avif)

The WMS layer will be added to the map and TOC after the project layer list.

**N.B.** the added WMS layer cannot not be queried.

The list of WMS services and the specific WMS layers added will remain available to the user until the browser cache is cleared.

#### TMS (URL)
The user can add one or more TMS services by defining:
 * **URL:** the TMS service URL
 * **Name:** custom name to associate with the service
 * **Projection system** to be associated
 * **Position** (top or buttom) with respect to the other layers of the project
 * **Opacity** of the layer

![Screenshot: G3wclient Add Tms](/img/manual-english-g3wclient-add-tms.avif)

The TMS layer will be added to the map and TOC after the project layer list.

**N.B.:** the added TMS layer cannot not be queried.

The list of TMS services and the specific WMS layers added will remain available to the user until the browser cache is cleared.

#### Local file

The user can add one or more local layer uploading it in the form.

The formats currently managed are:
 * gml
 * geojson
 * kml
 * kmz
 * gpx
 * csv
 * shapefile (zipped)

For each layer you need to specify:
 * associated **Projection** system
 * **Position** (top or buttom) with respect to the other layers of the project
 * **Persistent data:** keep the imported layer in this browser after reloading the page. If disabled, the layer is only available until you reload or close the page. This option does not publish the layer to other users.
 * **Label (optional):** the field to use to label the features
 * Layer **color** and **opacity**

![Screenshot: G3wclient Add Layer Local](/img/manual-english-g3wclient-add-layer-local.avif)

### Change map

Switch to another accessible map while keeping the current extent and scale.

Clicking this item will open a modal panel displaying other maps in the same Cartographic Group as the current map.

You can change the map view while maintaining the current scale and extent.

An arrow icon in the upper left corner will allow you to navigate between Cartographic Groups (and possibly Cartographic Macrogroups) to select other maps.

## Time series

**NB: the Time Series function is only available with a QGIS Server version >= 3.26**

This version of G3W-SUITE manages the temporal aspects for both vector and raster layers but with limitations:
 * **vector layers:** limited to the **Single field with Date/Time** configuration
 * **raster layers:** Mesh layer
 * **WMS-T**

 It is possible to create animations based on multiple temporal layers both raster and vector.

If in the QGIS project  a temporal vector/raster layer on which the **Dynamic temporal control** property has been activated is present, the client will show an additional panel called **Time series**.

This panel will allow you to:
 * define the start/end date of the time series
 * define the step of the animation
 * start and manage the temporal animation

![Screenshot: G3wclient Timeseries Tool](/img/manual-english-g3wclient-timeseries-tool.avif)

The modification of the start date of the series will determine the updating of the map with the visualization of the layer in coherence with the chosen date.

**Pay attention: to use the Time series function for raster data, it must also be activated at the level of the G3W-ADMIN layer properties.**

![Screenshot: G3wclient Timeseries Admin](/img/manual-english-g3wclient-timeseries-admin.avif)
## Branding

Customize the G3W-SUITE interface to match your organization's branding.

[Read online](/en/docs/branding/)

# Branding

Customize the G3W-SUITE interface to match your organization's branding.

Set branding options in `g3w-admin/base/settings/local_settings.py`. With the Docker stack, edit `config/g3w-suite/settings_docker.py` instead: Compose mounts it as `local_settings.py`.

- [Custom files](#g3wsuite_custom_static_url)
- [Logos](#logos)
- [Stylesheets and scripts](#stylesheets-and-scripts)
- [Map client appearance](#map-client-appearance)
- [Setting a default language](#setting-a-default-language)

## G3WSUITE_CUSTOM_STATIC_URL

Most of the style related settings depend on the ```G3WSUITE_CUSTOM_STATIC_URL``` attribute. This setting is a string that represents the URL from which **custom** static files are served. 

```python
G3WSUITE_CUSTOM_STATIC_URL = '/static/overrides/'
```

For this Docker example, put the custom files under `config/g3w-suite/overrides/static/`. Compose mounts that directory in NGINX, which serves it at `/static/overrides/`.

**NOTE:** When testing this in development/debug mode, the static folder **custom_static** needs to be created in the static folder of the **core** package of the g3w-admin app. 

```
g3w-admin/
└── core/
    └── static/
        └── custom_static/
            ├── css/
            │   └── custom.css
            ├── favicon.ico
            ├── logo_login.png
            ├── logo_main.png
            └── logo_reduced.png
```

In this case the setting needs to be adjusted to contain the static folder (note the initial static folder):

```python
G3WSUITE_CUSTOM_STATIC_URL = '/static/custom_static/'
```


## G3WSUITE_POWERD_BY

The powered by setting, turned on by default, shows information about the suite and the main developers behind it in the credits section, which is accessible from the top bar of the suite.

Without any interaction the section looks like this:

![Screenshot: Branding 01 Credits On](/img/manual-english-branding-01-credits-on.avif)

Adding the following line to the ```local_settings.py``` file will turn off the *powered by* section and show only what has been set in the **Map CLient Data** section of the **General Suite Data**:

```python
G3WSUITE_POWERD_BY=False
```

![Screenshot: Branding 02 Credits Off](/img/manual-english-branding-02-credits-off.avif)


## Logos

When it comes to logos, 4 images can be customized:

- **G3WSUITE_MAIN_LOGO**: The logo that appears in the top left corner of the suite when logged in the admin section. Mind that this one needs to be around 200x60 pixels to fit nicely.
- **G3WSUITE_RID_LOGO**: The logo that appears in the top left corner of the suite when logged in the admin section, with the sidebar reduced. Mind that this one needs to be around 60x60 pixels to fit nicely.
- **G3WSUITE_LOGIN_LOGO**: The logo that appears on the login screen.
- **G3WSUITE_FAVICON**: The favicon of the suite.

The settings for these images are strings that represent the path to the image, relative to the **G3WSUITE_CUSTOM_STATIC_URL** setting.

```python
G3WSUITE_FAVICON = G3WSUITE_CUSTOM_STATIC_URL + 'favicon.ico'
G3WSUITE_MAIN_LOGO = G3WSUITE_CUSTOM_STATIC_URL + 'logo_main.png'
G3WSUITE_RID_LOGO = G3WSUITE_CUSTOM_STATIC_URL + 'logo_reduced.png'
G3WSUITE_LOGIN_LOGO = G3WSUITE_CUSTOM_STATIC_URL + 'logo_login.png'
```

This will lead to a login page like this:

![Screenshot: Branding 08 Logos Login](/img/manual-english-branding-08-logos-login.avif)

and to the following admin logo icon:

![Screenshot: Branding 09 Logos Main](/img/manual-english-branding-09-logos-main.avif)

and its reduced form:

![Screenshot: Branding 10 Logos Reduced](/img/manual-english-branding-10-logos-reduced.avif)

## G3WSUITE_CUSTOM_TITLE

This setting overrides the browser tab title in the administration panel and the title prefix in the map client. The client appends the project title.

![Screenshot: Branding 03 Html Title Off](/img/manual-english-branding-03-html-title-off.avif)

By setting the following line in the ```local_settings.py``` file:

```python
G3WSUITE_CUSTOM_TITLE = "The Etruscan Webgis for the masses"
```

we get the following result:

![Screenshot: Branding 04 Html Title On](/img/manual-english-branding-04-html-title-on.avif)

## Stylesheets and scripts

### G3WSUITE_CUSTOM_CSS

`G3WSUITE_CUSTOM_CSS` is a list of stylesheet URLs. The client and administration templates load this list when `G3WSUITE_CUSTOM_STATIC_URL` is set:

```python
G3WSUITE_CUSTOM_CSS = [
    G3WSUITE_CUSTOM_STATIC_URL +'css/custom.css'
]
```

This custom css can be used to override some default suite css settings and allows for some great customization.

Use the project settings to control which map tools are available. For visual changes, inspect the current client markup before writing selectors; element IDs can change between releases.

#### Example: change the skin color

To change the skin color of the suite, you can add the following css to the custom css file:

```css
body #app {
    --skin-color: #f50000;
}
```

This changes the map client's accent color to red.

![Screenshot: Branding 13 Css Skin](/img/manual-english-branding-13-css-skin.avif)

### `G3WSUITE_CUSTOM_JS`
A list of custom js files added to `admin` pages and to the `client`.
Mandatory is set `G3WSUITE_CUSTOM_STATIC_URL`.
I.e.

~~~
G3WSUITE_CUSTOM_JS = [
    G3WSUITE_CUSTOM_STATIC_URL +'js/custom.js'
]
~~~

## Map client appearance

### G3W_CLIENT_SEARCH_TITLE

The search section title in the webgis client can be customized by setting the following line in the ```local_settings.py``` file:

```python
G3W_CLIENT_SEARCH_TITLE = "Search for the Holy Grail"
```

This will help user to search for the Holy Grail:

![Screenshot: Branding 17 Search Title](/img/manual-english-branding-17-search-title.avif)

### G3W_CLIENT_HEADER_CUSTOM_LINKS

The header custom links setting is a list of dictionaries that represent links that will be shown in the top bar of the webgis client. Each dictionary creates a new button,
using the icon and as tooltip the title of the dictionary.

There can be two type of links, **url** and **modal**. The **url** type opens a new tab using the url provided in the dictionary, while the **modal** type opens a modal dialog containing the content provided in the dictionary.

```python
G3W_CLIENT_HEADER_CUSTOM_LINKS = [
    {
        'url': 'https://gis3w.it',
        'title': 'Gis3W company',
        'i18n': True,
        'target': '_blank',
        'img': 'https://gis3w.it/wp-content/uploads/2016/10/logo_qgis-1-100x100.png?x22227'
    },
    {
        "title": "Firefox me!",
        "content": "<div style='position: fixed; top: 10vh; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); background: white; width: 60%; max-width: 600px; min-height: 200px; max-height: 80vh; padding: 20px; border-radius: 10px; box-shadow: 0px 4px 10px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3); text-align: center; overflow: auto;'><img src='https://img.icons8.com/external-those-icons-flat-those-icons/96/external-Firefox-logos-and-brands-those-icons-flat-those-icons.png' style='width: 50px; margin-bottom: 10px;' /><p>Html example content to show in modal</p></div>",
        "type": "modal",
        "position": 10,
        "img": "https://img.icons8.com/external-those-icons-flat-those-icons/96/external-Firefox-logos-and-brands-those-icons-flat-those-icons.png"
    },
]
```

The **i18n** key is used to translate the title of the link. If set to True, the title will be translated (if possible) using the suite's translation system.

The above example creates changes the top bar from:

![Screenshot: Branding 05 Header Links Off](/img/manual-english-branding-05-header-links-off.avif)

to:

![Screenshot: Branding 06 Header Links On](/img/manual-english-branding-06-header-links-on.avif)

While ths first link opens a new tab with the Gis3W company website, the second link opens a modal dialog like this:

![Screenshot: Branding 07 Header Links Click](/img/manual-english-branding-07-header-links-click.avif)


### G3W_CLIENT_RIGHT_PANEL

The right panel width can be set with the following setting:

```python
G3W_CLIENT_RIGHT_PANEL = {
    'width': 50
}
```

The width is a percentage of the map view (45% by default).


### G3W_CLIENT_LEGEND

Customize the WebGIS client legend with these settings:

```python
G3W_CLIENT_LEGEND = {
    "layerfontsize": 20, # layer title font size
    "itemfontsize": 16, # legend rules font size
    'color': 'black', # all text font color
    'transparent': False, # if false, makes a white background
    'boxspace': 10,  # insets around legend
    "layerspace": 8, # space between layers
    'layertitlespace': 4, # space between layer title and rules
    'symbolspace': 4, # spacing between rules
    'iconlabelspace': 5, # spacing between icon and rule name
    'symbolwidth': 18, # width of the icon
    'symbolheight': 4,  # height of the icon
    "showfeaturecount": True  # show the number of features in the legend
}
```

This would change the legend from:

![Screenshot: Branding 19 Legend Off](/img/manual-english-branding-19-legend-off.avif)

to:


![Screenshot: Branding 18 Legend](/img/manual-english-branding-18-legend.avif)

## Setting a default language


Set `LANGUAGE_CODE` in the same settings file to change Django's fallback language:

```python
LANGUAGE_CODE = 'it'
```

This is a fallback, not a way to force one language for all visitors. Django can still select a supported language from the URL, the language cookie or the browser preferences.
## Cartographic groups

Manage existing Cartographic Groups or create new ones.

[Read online](/en/docs/cartographic-groups/)

# Cartographic groups

## Cartographic Groups
_**Manage existing Cartographic Groups or create new ones.**_

A Cartographic Group is create  to **collect a series of cartographic projects belonging, for example, to the same theme** (Urban Planning Regulations, tourist maps ...) and characterized by the same projection system.

You can switch between WebGIS services while keeping the map extent and scale only when their projects belong to the same cartographic group.

In the left side menu there is the **Cartographic Groups** item with two sub-items:
 * **Add Group:** to create a new Cartographic Group
 * **Group List:** to access the list of groups present

You can also access the list of groups by clicking on the **"Show"** button in the **Cartographic Groups** box on the **Dashboard**.

### Add Group
**Through this item, available only for the Admin or Editor1 users, it is possible to create a new Cartographic Group.**

During creation, some functional characteristics and tools that the WebGis interface will show for all cartographic projects published within the group are also defined.

Let's see in detail the various sub-sessions of the group creation form.

#### General data
 * **`Name *`:** a generic internal identification name (not show in the front end)
 * **`Title`***: descriptive title of the Group (will appear in the list of Cartographic Groups)
 * **`Description`**: description of the content
 * **`Language`***: interface language
 
#### Logo/Picture
 * **`Header logo img`***: the logo to be displayed in the header del client cartografico
 * **`Use logo image for client`** option
 * **`Logo link`:** a eventual link to associate with the logo
 
 **REMEBER**
 
By default, the map client header, for each WebGis service, is composed of:
 * main title (if set at General Data management level)
 * logo and title associated with the **Cartographic Group**
 * title of the WebGis service

If you select the **Use MacroGroup title and logo for the client** options, the map client header, for each WebGis service, will instead consist of:
 * main title (if set at General Data management level)
 * logo and title associated with the **Cartographic MacroGroup**
 * title of the WebGis service
 
 If you select the **Use Group logo for the client** options, the map client header, for each WebGis service, will instead consist of:
 * main title (if set at General Data management level)
 * title associated with the **Cartographic MacroGroup**
 * logo associated with the **Cartographic Group** (if MacroGroup logo option is active this options takes precedence)
 * title of the WebGis service
     
#### ACL Users
**Access and modification powers are managed.**

The options present will vary according to the type of user (Admin or Editor1) who creates/manages the Group

**Remember:** the presence of users of Editor1 and Editor2 roles is not mandatory and therefore the respective sub-sessions are optional.

Learn more about this in the [dedicated session](webgis-roles-and-organization.md).

Let’s see in detail the various sub-sessions of the ACL Users session:
 * **`Editor1 User`:** defines the **user (Editor1) manager of the Group**.
     The entry is present only when the Admin type user creates the Group
     If the Group is created by a user associated with the Editor1 role this option is not visible and the Group is associated directly with that user
 * **`Editor2 User`:** defines the **user (Editor2) manager of the Group**.
 * **`Viewers users`:** define the individual **users (Viewers) who have the credentials to view the contents of the group**. By choosing the anonymous user (AnonymousUser) the group will be visible and accessible by AnonymousUser
 * **`Editor user groups`:** define the **user groups (Editor2) who manage the Group**.
 * **`Viewer user groups`:** you define the **user groups (Viewer) which have the credentials to view the contents of the group**.

The option **`Propagate viewers user (single and groups) permissions`** allows you to propagate the Viewer users (individuals and/or groups) associated to the Group to ALL the WebGis services present in it. 

**Be careful: this option cancels any differentiation in the access policies applied to the WebGis services contained in the Group.**

![Screenshot: G3W-SUITE Administration Group Add ACL](/img/manual-english-g3wsuite-administration-group-add-acl.avif)

#### MacroGroups
**Possible definition of the belonging MacroGroup.**

This option is available only if Cartographic macro groups have been created

In the event that the Group is created by an Editor1 type user, the Group will be automatically associated with the MacroGroup associated with the same Editor1.

#### GEO data
**Projection system associated with the group.**

**N.B.** All projects loaded into the group must be associated with this SRID.

#### Base layers and Map interaction tools
In this box you can define:
 * **`Mapcontrols`***: list of tools available on the WebGis client:
   * **zoomtoextent:** zoom to the initial extension
   * **zoom:** zoom in and zoom out
   * **zoombox:** zoom tool based on drawing a rectangle
   * **query:** puntual query of geographical layers
   * **querybbox:** query via bounding box (**N.B. it is necessary that the layers are published as WFS services on the QGIS project**)
   * **querybypolygon:** it will be possible to automatically query the features of one or more layers that fall inside a polygonal element of a guide layer. (Eg what's inside a cadastral parcel?) - **N.B. it is necessary that the all the layers involved in this kind of query are published as WFS services on the QGIS project**
   * **querybydrawpolygon:** query based on a polygon drawn on the map  (**N.B. it is necessary that the layers are published as WFS services on the QGIS project**) 
   * **zoomhistory:** undo/redo tools to navigate previous and post visualization areas
   * **overview:** presence of a panoramic map
   * **scaleline:** presence of the scale bar
   * **scale:** tool for defining the display scale
   * **mouseposition:** display of mouse position coordinates
   * **geolocation:** geolocation tool  (available only with https certificate)
   * **geocoding:** address search tools and toponyms based on OSM; see the [dedicated paragraph](geocoding.md) for using map control as a tool for populating project data
   * **streetview:** due to Google polycy, StreetView it will open on a new browse tab without the aspects of synchronization with the map
   * **length:** linear measuring instrument
   * **area:** surface measuring instrument
   * **addlayers:** tool for temporarily uploading GML, GeoJson, KML, GPX, SHP (zipped) and CSV with coordinate to WebGis. These layers will remain until the end of the work session
   * **screenshot:*** tool to take a screenshot of the map area
   * **geoscreenshot:*** tool to create a GeoTIFF of the map area
   * **annotation:*** an useful tool to add custom texts or geometrics (points, line, cirlce, polygon) annotations to the map and share them
 * **`Baselayer`:** choice of the base maps that will be available on the WebGis client
 * **`Background color`:** choice of the background color of the maps (default white)
 
***NB:** the security protocols prevent the creation of screenshots if WMS services with domains other than the publication one are present on the map. **In this case the icons will not be present on the client even if the MapControl is selected.**
To avoid this, set the WMS as **internal WMS** in the [Widget management](layer-tools.md) section.

![Screenshot: G3W-SUITE Administration Group Add Geodata](/img/manual-english-g3wsuite-administration-group-add-geodata.avif)

The bundled base-layer data includes **OpenStreetMap** and **Bing** presets. Check current provider licensing before enabling Bing or Google base maps; a preset in the administration panel does not itself grant permission to use a service.

Remember that it is possible to build customized Base Layers starting from open external Base Layer or from the contenents of a projects published on the suite.

In this regard, consult the section on [**base layers**](group-base-layers-and-languages.md).


#### Copyright
**`Terms of use`:** description of the terms of use of the map and any other info
**`Link to terms`:** link to text

After filling in the various form, click on the **Save** button to confirm your choices.
 
![Button: Save](/img/manual-english-buttom-save.avif)

[Manage cartographic groups](manage-cartographic-groups.md)
## Components of G3W-SUITE

This manual follows G3W-ADMIN 3.11.4, which ships with G3W-CLIENT 4.1.5. For Docker deployments, use the v3.11.x branch of G3W-SUITE-DOCKER.

[Read online](/en/docs/components-of-g3w-suite/)

# Components of G3W-SUITE

## Versions and compatibility

This manual follows G3W-ADMIN 3.11.4, which ships with G3W-CLIENT 4.1.5. For Docker deployments, use the `v3.11.x` branch of G3W-SUITE-DOCKER.

[Compare supported versions and their requirements](versions-and-compatibility.md).

For technical background, see the generated DeepWiki pages for [G3W-CLIENT](https://deepwiki.com/g3w-suite/g3w-client), [G3W-ADMIN](https://deepwiki.com/g3w-suite/g3w-admin) and [G3W-SUITE-DOCKER](https://deepwiki.com/g3w-suite/g3w-suite-docker). They may describe a different revision; follow this manual for the stable release.

## Technological infrastructure

The publishing system is based on a series of OS tools and software

* **`PostgreSQL/PostGis`**: for the management of application data
* **`PostgreSQL/PostGis` or `SpatiaLite`**: for the management of geographic data
* **`QGIS Server LTR`** as OGC services server
* **`G3W-ADMIN` - the Administration component**: developed in **`Python`** using **`Django`**
* **`G3W-CLIENT` - the map client**: built with **OpenLayers 10** and **Vue 2**
* The main libraries used for the management and the visualization of the geographical part and the interaction with the user are: **`OpenLayer, Boostrap, jQuery, Lodash` and `Vue.js`**.
* **`Gulp.js`** as task runner

```mermaid G3W-CLIENT exchanges REST and OGC requests with G3W-ADMIN, which uses PostgreSQL, PostGIS and QGIS Server
flowchart TB
  client["G3W-CLIENT<br/>OpenLayers + Vue.js"]
  admin["G3W-ADMIN<br/>Django"]
  app[("PostgreSQL<br/>Application data")]
  geo[("PostgreSQL + PostGIS<br/>Geographic data")]
  server["QGIS Server"]
  client <-->|REST API| admin
  client <-->|OGC services| admin
  admin <--> app
  admin <--> geo
  admin <-->|OWS proxy| server
  server <--> geo
```

Below is a diagram relating to the standard workflow

```mermaid A publisher uploads a QGIS project and sets its permissions; the web client initializes through G3W-ADMIN, which then proxies OGC requests to QGIS Server
sequenceDiagram
  actor Publisher as Publisher
  participant Client as G3W-CLIENT
  participant Admin as G3W-ADMIN
  participant Server as QGIS Server
  Publisher->>Admin: Upload QGIS project and configure permissions and options
  Note right of Admin: Store project and layer information in the database
  Client->>Admin: Request initial project configuration
  Admin->>Server: GetProjectSettings
  Server-->>Admin: Additional project information
  Admin-->>Client: Stored and retrieved project configuration
  Client->>Admin: Request OGC service
  Admin->>Server: Forward OWS request
  Server-->>Admin: OWS response
  Admin-->>Client: Forward OWS response
```

## G3W-ADMIN

![G3W-ADMIN administration interface](/img/manual-english-g3wadmin-django-administration.avif)

G3W-ADMIN is the Django server application at the core of G3W-SUITE. It publishes web maps from QGIS projects and provides the administration tools to manage them.

### Publish and administer

Publish QGIS projects through QGIS Server, organize them into cartographic groups, and manage users, groups, permissions and project settings.

### Extend the platform

Optional modules add capabilities such as QGIS Processing integration and authentication through public-sector services.

[View the G3W-ADMIN source repository](https://github.com/g3w-suite/g3w-admin) · [Read the administration guide](/en/docs/publish-and-update-webgis-services/)

## G3W-CLIENT

![G3W-CLIENT web map interface](/img/manual-english-g3wclient-interface.avif)

G3W-CLIENT is the browser-based map application for exploring and working with data published by G3W-SUITE.

### Explore and work with maps

Use map navigation, search, identify and query tools, print layouts, charts and data tables. When enabled for a project, users can also edit features and related records directly in the browser.

### Adapted to each project

The client uses the QGIS project configuration for layers, forms, styles and map content, and supports responsive use on desktop and mobile devices.

[View the G3W-CLIENT source repository](https://github.com/g3w-suite/g3w-client) · [Read the client guide](/en/docs/map-client/)

## G3W-ADMIN-PROCESSING

![QGIS Processing model builder](/img/site-g3wsuite-processing.avif)

G3W-ADMIN-PROCESSING integrates QGIS Processing models with G3W-SUITE, making selected geoprocessing workflows available through the web client.

### Run processing models

Administrators can upload QGIS `.model3` files and configure them for execution. Depending on the model and deployment, jobs can run synchronously or in batches.

The module is an optional extension and requires a compatible G3W-SUITE installation and QGIS Processing environment.

[View the G3W-ADMIN-PROCESSING source repository](https://github.com/g3w-suite/g3w-admin-processing) · [Read about Processing in the manual](/en/docs/)

## G3W-SUITE-DOCKER

```mermaid G3W-SUITE publication flow: QGIS projects are uploaded to G3W-ADMIN, which uses QGIS Server to serve maps to G3W-CLIENT
flowchart LR
  project["QGIS project"] -->|Upload and configure| admin["G3W-ADMIN"]
  admin <-->|GetProjectSettings / OWS| server["QGIS Server"]
  admin <-->|REST / OGC| client["G3W-CLIENT"]
```

G3W-SUITE-DOCKER provides a Docker-based deployment stack for running G3W-SUITE and its supporting services.

### Run the platform with containers

The stack brings together the application, QGIS Server, NGINX and PostgreSQL/PostGIS services. It is a starting point for self-hosted deployments; production environments should be configured and maintained for their own operational requirements.

Use the [Quick Start guide](/en/docs/quick-start/) to publish a first project and the [Docker documentation](/en/docs/docker-installation/) for setup details.

[View the G3W-SUITE-DOCKER source repository](https://github.com/g3w-suite/g3w-suite-docker)

## G3W-ADMIN-PORTAL

![G3W-SUITE public portal](/img/manual-english-g3wsuite-portal-frontend.avif)

G3W-ADMIN-PORTAL is an optional portal for presenting published cartographic groups through a public-facing interface.

### A branded entry point

The frontend can provide a separate landing page for an organization, helping visitors find and open the WebGIS projects made available to them.

It complements the G3W-ADMIN publishing tools and can be adapted to the identity and needs of a deployment.

[View the G3W-ADMIN-PORTAL source repository](https://github.com/g3w-suite/g3w-admin-portal)

## G3W-ADMIN-PDND

![G3W-SUITE login screen](/img/manual-english-socialauth-login-screen.avif)

G3W-ADMIN-PDND is an optional integration for connecting G3W-SUITE to Italy's Public Digital Data Platform (PDND) authentication services.

### Authentication for public services

The integration supports authentication through PDND voucher tokens. It is intended for deployments that need to connect their G3W-SUITE instance with public-sector services.

This component is released under the MIT licence. Check its repository for installation requirements and configuration details.

[View the G3W-ADMIN-PDND source repository](https://github.com/g3w-suite/g3w-admin-pdnd)

## Collaborative editing

![G3W-CLIENT editing tools](/img/manual-english-editing-client-tool.avif)

G3W-SUITE's editing tools let authorized users update geographic features and related records from the web client, using forms and rules configured in QGIS.

### Work together on geographic data

Editing can be enabled for selected layers and user groups. Geometry, attributes and relations can be managed in the browser, while feature locks help prevent conflicting edits by multiple users.

The editing capabilities are maintained in the G3W-ADMIN and G3W-CLIENT projects rather than in a separate plugin repository.

[Read the editing guide](/en/docs/editing-tools/)

## Configure charts

View plots created using QGIS DataPlotly (a great plugin developed by Matteo Ghetta) in the cartographic client.

[Read online](/en/docs/configure-charts/)

# Configure charts

## ![Icon: Dataplotly](/img/manual-english-icon-dataplotly.avif) QPlotly widget

### Activate charts on your WebGis

**View plots created using QGIS [DataPlotly](https://github.com/ghtmtt/DataPlotly) (a great plugin developed by [Matteo Ghetta](https://github.com/ghtmtt)) in the cartographic client.**

The module, based on the [Plotly library](https://plotly.com/), , manages plots builts and saved as xml in the DataPlotly QGIS plugin.

At the level of the layer for which the charts has been prepared, click on the **QPlotly widgets** icon ![Icon: Dataplotly](/img/manual-english-icon-dataplotly.avif) and load the xml by clicking on the **'New Qplotly widget'** button.

As with searches, the uploaded graph will now be available in all projects that contain the same layer. As with searches, to activate the graph in other projects, access the layer and check the **'Linked'** checkbox.

After loading the XML file, the loaded chart will be listed, and icons and checkboxes will allow you to select its display modes:
 * **Edit icon:** to reload the XML file after editing the chart in QGIS
 * **Delete icon:** to delete the chart (deleted for all similar layers, even in other projects)
 * **Download icon:** to download the XML
 * **Related widgets icon:** to create multiple charts (see the dedicated section below)
 * **Active at startup checkbox:** to define whether the chart should be active when accessing the Charts menu in the web client
 * **Position drop-down menu:** to define whether the chart should be displayed in the client sidebar, associated with the queried feature (Query), related to data from a 1:N relationship, or in both positions (Sidebar, Query)

For each chart, the following information is displayed:
 * **Title:** defined in the DataPltly plugin
 * **Type:** chart type
 * **Linked checkbox:** to activate/deactivate the chart without removing it
 
![Screenshot: Charts Admin](/img/manual-english-charts-admin.avif)

It is also possible:
 * **download the plot XML file** to reuse it in QGIS
 * **define the activation status** of the plots when the WebGis service is started

![Screenshot: G3W-SUITE Administration Plots](/img/manual-english-g3wsuite-administration-plots.avif)

The chart title comes from the DataPlotly plugin and is used as its label in G3W-SUITE.

In the client, **filter charts by features visible on the map or selected by the user**.

![Screenshot: G3W-SUITE QGIS Plots](/img/manual-english-g3wsuite-qgis-plots.avif)
![Screenshot: G3W-SUITE Client Plots](/img/manual-english-g3wsuite-client-plots.avif)

### Multiple charts

The QGIS DataPlotly plugin does not allow you to export the XML of multiple overlapping graphs.

In G3W-SUITE, you can associate two or more graphs to display them as overlapping graphs on the client.

Steps to create a multiple graph:
 * access the list of graphs associated with a specific layer
 * click the Related widgets icon for one of the graphs to which you want to associate other graphs
 * in the window, add the graphs that will make up the multiple graph from those already present and associated with the layer
 * sort the graphs to define their display order (the title shown will be the one associated with the first graph in the list).
 
![Screenshot: Charts Admin Multicharts](/img/manual-english-charts-admin-multicharts.avif)

### Charts based on 1:N data relation (child layer)

If the chart is linked to a child layer in a 1:N relation, it can also be displayed at the information level of the individual parent features and in the display of the table of related children.

![Screenshot: G3wclient Fomr 1 N Plots](/img/manual-english-g3wclient-fomr-1-n-plots.avif)

![Screenshot: Charts On Childs](/img/manual-english-charts-on-childs.avif)

### Chart visibility
Graphs based on child layers/tables of a 1:N relations are visible both in the main graphs menu and associated with the attributes of a feature of the parent layer (for the relations-limited records).

Admin side, via the ‘Position’ drop-down menù, it is now possible to define whether these graphs should be displayed:
 * **Sidebar:** only on the main chart panel
 * **Query:** only associated with parent attributes only at the parent feature attribute level
 * **Sidebar, Query:** in both positions (default)

### Chart order
On the Admin side it is possible to define the display order of the graphs, associated with the WebGis service, within the Charts panel of the cartographic client.

To access the configuration menu, click on the **'Project QPlotly widgets order'** icon ![Icon: Chart Order](/img/manual-english-icon-chart-order.avif)

You can use Drag&Drop to define the order on the widget list

![Screenshot: Chart Order Settings](/img/manual-english-chart-order-settings.avif)

## Demo tutorial

**_The tutorial is based on a QGIS project dedicated to the management of a layer representing a series of buildings located on the territory._**

**_In addition to the geographical aspects, the project involves the management of numerous and diversified attributes and of the related maintenance interventions through a 1: n type relation._**

In this tutorial you will:
* customize the various graphic-functional aspects of the basic project
* publish the project as a WebGis service
* create personalized searches
* add plots made with DataPlotly QGIS plugin
* activate the editing functionality by customizing associated forms and widgets

![Screenshot: Demo Webgis Project](/img/manual-english-demo-webgis-project.avif)

## Download demo data

The tutorial is based on predefined data and QGIS 3.44.x LTR project **downloadable from [this link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Xpx1FvTNWtx74maXe7jatU_GgyC8QlpB/view?usp=sharing)**.

The .zip file contains the **`G3W-SUITE`** directory with three sub directories:
* **`projects`:** containing a QGIS project (**`public-buildings-management-demo-310.qgs`**) already optimized for the tutorial
* **`project_data/spatialite`**: containing a SpatiaLite DB with basic data (**`build_management_demo.sqlite`**)
* **`plots`**: containing a a series of plots created with the **DataPlotly** plugin and saved in xml format

![Screenshot: Demo Zip File](/img/manual-english-demo-zip-file.avif)

Inside the **`build_management_demo.sqlite` SpatiaLite DB** there are the following layers:
* **`buildings` (polygon layer):** reference layer for editing aspects
* **`maintenance_works` (alphanumeric table):** with the maintenance interventions associated with the individual buildings
* **`buildings_rating` (alphanumeric table):** with the annual assessments relating to individual buildings
* **`roads` (linear layer):** layer to define the address associated to any buildings
* **`work_areas` (polygon layer):** with the perimeter of work areas to be used to define any geo-constraints
* **`type_subtype` (alphanumeric table):** a decoding table of the type and subtype values associated with the individual buildings

**IMPORTANT: a copy of this data are present on the server, you can not change your local data copy**

The project (**based on QGIS LTR 3.44.x**) foresees:
* a **dressing categorized by the `buildings` layer** based on the categorical field **`type`**
* the presence of a **1: n relation** between the **`buildings`** layer and the alphanumeric **`maintenance_works`** and **`buildings_rating`** tables
* pre-developed **query forms** for the **`buildings`** layer and the **`maintenance_works`** table
* predefined **editing widgets** for the fields of the two main layers: **`buildings`** , **`maintenance_works`** and **`buildings_rating`** tables
* two standard **print layout** and an two **atlas print layout** based on buildgs layer features


![Screenshot: Demo QGIS Project](/img/manual-english-demo-qgis-project.avif)

### Modify the QGIS project title

The publication system provides for the use of the **title of the project** as the **unique identifier of the WebGis service**.

**So, before publishing the project, it will be NECESSARY to change the title associated with the basic project (`Project -> Properties ... - Session: General`)**

![Screenshot: Qgisserver Change Title](/img/manual-english-qgisserver-change-title.avif)

- [Publish and update a service](publish-a-webgis-service.md)
- [Try layer tools in the demo](try-layer-tools-in-the-demo.md)
- [Online editing](try-online-editing.md)
## Docker environment variables

Set these environment variables when deploying G3W-SUITE with Docker.

[Read online](/en/docs/docker-environment-variables/)

# Docker environment variables

Set these environment variables when deploying G3W-SUITE with [Docker](https://github.com/g3w-suite/g3w-suite-docker).

Add them to the deployment `.env` file. Compose must also pass each variable to the service that uses it.

These notes describe the Docker `v3.11.x` branch; its `.env.example` and Compose files are not interchangeable with development-branch configuration.

## Requirements variables

### `WEBGIS_PUBLIC_HOSTNAME`

The domain to which the application will respond.

### `WEBGIS_DOCKER_SHARED_VOLUME`

The path on which the docker permanent volume will be mounted with the application data inside.

### Database connections parameters

The follow variables re for set the connection to G3W-SUITE administration database.

### `G3WSUITE_POSTGRES_USER_LOCAL`
Database username to connect to G3W-SUITE database.
If you are going to use docker postgis image, it'll be created on first run of container.

### `G3WSUITE_POSTGRES_PASS`
Database username password to connect to G3W-SUITE database.
If you are going to use docker postgis image, it'll be created on first run of container.

### `G3WSUITE_POSTGRES_DBNAME`
Database name of G3W-SUITE database connect to.
If you are going to use docker postgis image, it'll be created on first run of container.

### `G3WSUITE_POSTGRES_HOST`
Database host value connect to.
If you are going to use docker postgis image, it'll be set to `postgis`

### `G3WSUITE_POSTGRES_PORT`
Database port value connect to.
If you are going to use docker postgis image, it'll be set to `5432`

### `G3WSUITE_ADMIN_USERNAME`
The login used for the superuser account. Only works when setup a new environment.

### `G3WSUITE_ADMIN_PASSWORD`
The password used during initial setup. If `docker-compose.yml` passes `G3WSUITE_ADMIN_PASS` instead, correct `services.g3w-suite.environment` as shown in the [installation guide](docker-installation.md#run). The optional Huey stack already passes `G3WSUITE_ADMIN_PASSWORD`.

## Other not required settings

### Caching system

### `TILESTACHE_CACHE_TOKEN`
A custom unique token to use for internal caching request.
The Docker example settings provide a shared fallback token; set a unique value for each deployment.

### `TILESTACHE_CACHE_BUFFER_SIZE`
Tile width/height tile map dimension.
Default value is: `256`.

### `G3WSUITE_TILECACHE_PATH`
Internal path to folder to save tiles of map.
Dafault value is: `/shared-volume/tile_cache/`.

### Gunicorn settings

G3W-SUITE with docker is deployed with Gunicorn.

### `G3WSUITE_GUNICORN_NUM_WORKERS`
Number of workers Gunicorn has to start with.
Default: `8`.
Usually then number of workers is equal to number of processor x 2.

### `G3WSUITE_GUNICORN_MAX_REQUESTS`
Number of requests after that gunicorn worker restart.
Default: `200`.
Thi is used to compensate the python/gunicorn memory leaks.

The Gunicorn configuration is created in the shared volume on first startup and is not overwritten on later starts. The generated file reads these environment variables; review `/shared-volume/gunicorn.conf.py` if it has been customized.

### QGIS server variables

QGIS environment variables can be set as described in the [QGIS Server manual](https://docs.qgis.org/3.44/en/docs/server_manual/config.html#environment-variables); add them to the relevant Compose service.

The following varaible are just set into docker-compose files:

### `PGSERVICEFILE`
Put your pg services into `./secrets/pg_service.conf`, the conf file will be mounted into
docker container at runtime to PGSERVICEFILE path position.

### `QGIS_SERVER_LOG_FILE`

### `QGIS_SERVER_LOG_LEVEL`

### Openrouteservice

The `v3.11.x` example `.env` lists `ORS_API_ENDPOINT`, `ORS_API_KEY`, `ORS_MAX_RANGES` and `ORS_MAX_LOCATIONS`, but the Compose files pass differently named endpoint and key variables and the mounted Docker settings do not read them. Configure the corresponding Django settings in `config/g3w-suite/settings_docker.py` instead; see [Openrouteservice settings](settings.md#openrouteservice-settings).

### Frontend module

### `FRONTEND`
If `true`, the startup script activates the bundled `frontend` module in the mounted settings on first activation.
## Docker installation

This repository contains scripts and recipes for deploy of the G3W-SUITE web-gis application with Docker and Docker compose .

[Read online](/en/docs/docker-installation/)

# Docker installation

This repository contains scripts and recipes for deploy of the G3W-SUITE web-gis application with Docker and Docker compose .

## Server sizing

CPU, memory and storage needs depend on the number of users, the complexity of the maps, the data and the enabled services. This guide does not prescribe a universal minimum: test the deployment with representative projects and concurrent users before choosing production capacity.

Monitor container CPU and memory usage with `docker stats`. Check free space on the shared volume with `df -h <shared-volume-path>`; allow room for the database, project data, uploads, tile cache and backups.

For a cloud deployment, choose a Linux host that supports the required Docker images and Docker Compose. Use persistent storage, plan backups and provide a domain and HTTPS for public access.

## Deploy

Use `docker-compose.yml` for a standard installation of G3W-SUITE 3.11.

Clone the stable Docker branch and enter its directory:

```bash
git clone --branch v3.11.x https://github.com/g3w-suite/g3w-suite-docker.git
cd g3w-suite-docker
```

### Configuration 

Create a file `.env` (or copy `.env.example` and rename it in `.env`) and place it in the main directory, the file
will contain the database credentials (change `<your password>`) and other settings:

```bash
# External hostname, for docker internal network aliases
WEBGIS_PUBLIC_HOSTNAME=demo.g3wsuite.it

# This volume is persistent and mounted by all
# containers as /shared-volume
WEBGIS_DOCKER_SHARED_VOLUME=./shared-volume

# Super User account
G3WSUITE_ADMIN_USERNAME=admin
G3WSUITE_ADMIN_PASSWORD=<your_password>

# DB setup
G3WSUITE_POSTGRES_USER_LOCAL=g3wsuite
G3WSUITE_POSTGRES_PASS=<your_password>
G3WSUITE_POSTGRES_DBNAME=g3wsuite
G3WSUITE_POSTGRES_HOST=postgis
G3WSUITE_POSTGRES_PORT=5432

PGSERVICEFILE=/pg_service/pg_service.conf
```

Description of other *environment variables* that can be used, are available on [Docker environment variables](docker-environment-variables.md)

### Run

Before the first start, check `services.g3w-suite.environment` in `docker-compose.yml`. If it lists `G3WSUITE_ADMIN_PASS`, replace that entry with `G3WSUITE_ADMIN_PASSWORD` so the setup script receives the password from `.env`.

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

Open http://localhost:8080. If the site does not respond, check the service status and the startup logs:

```bash
docker compose ps -a
docker compose logs --tail=100 g3w-suite postgis
```

![Login Page](/img/installation-english-login-page.avif)

## Optional Huey worker

Use the alternative `docker-compose-consumer.yml` only if you need the Huey worker for background jobs. It defines a complete stack, not an override. If you choose it, pass `-f docker-compose-consumer.yml` to subsequent Compose commands as well.

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose-consumer.yml up -d
```

## Builds

Docker compose will download images from docker hub (https://hub.docker.com/u/g3wsuite), 
but is also possible build main image of G3W-SUITE and other docker-compose images. 

#### G3W-SUITE

The main suite docker image can be built with:

```bash
docker build --build-arg G3W_SUITE_BRANCH=v.3.11.x -f Dockerfile.g3wsuite.dockerfile -t g3wsuite/g3w-suite:local-v3.11 .
```

The build argument selects the stable admin branch. Without it, the setup script clones `dev`, even when using the stable Docker checkout. The Dockerfile uses the `g3wsuite/g3w-suite-deps-ltr:v3.11.x` base image.

To run a locally built image, change the image tag for `g3w-suite` and, if you use the optional worker, for `g3w-suite-consumer` as well.

#### Postgis

The stable Compose files use `kartoza/postgis:16-3.4`.

## Setups

### PG_SERVICE

To use of PostgreSql Service, put your service setups into `./secrets/pg_service.conf`,
the conf file will be mounted into docker container at runtime to PGSERVICEFILE path position.

### HTTPS additional setup

For HTTPS, configure the hostname in `.env` and `config/nginx/nginx.conf`, including the administrator email in the latter. Ensure the domain resolves to the server and HTTP port 80 reaches the Nginx port 8080 for the ACME challenge; the provided Compose file publishes 8080, not 80.

With the HTTP configuration running, obtain a certificate before switching the includes in `config/nginx/nginx.conf` from `django` to `django_ssl` and restarting the selected stack. The repository's `run_certbot.sh` invokes an interactive container and recreates the default Compose stack, not the consumer stack; adapt and test certificate issuance and renewal for your deployment rather than assuming it works unattended in cron.


### Volumes

Data, projects, uploads and the database are stored in a shared mounted volume `shared-volume`, the volume should be on a persistent storage device and a backup
policy must be enforced.

The stable `.env.example` uses `./shared-volume`. Set `WEBGIS_DOCKER_SHARED_VOLUME` in `.env` to a persistent location suitable for production.

### First time setup

Set a strong administrator password in `.env` before starting a new installation. The `.env.example` file contains example credentials that must be changed.

Sign in to the administration panel with `G3WSUITE_ADMIN_USERNAME` and `G3WSUITE_ADMIN_PASSWORD`. Setup runs only once per shared volume and sets passwords on existing users as well; use a fresh database and volume for a new installation. After initialization, change passwords in the administration interface, not by editing `.env`.

### Caching

Tile cache can be configured and cleared per-layer through the webgis admin panel and lasts forever until it is disabled or cleared.

> Tip: enable cache on linestring and polygon layers.

### Editing

Editing module is active by default, to avoid simultaneous feature editing by two or more users, the editing module works with a feature lock system.
Without the Huey worker, schedule lock cleanup on the host. The command removes locks older than four hours by default. With Huey enabled, the editing module already schedules this cleanup periodically.

```
0 * * * * cd /path/to/g3w-suite-docker && docker compose exec -T g3w-suite python3 /code/g3w-admin/manage.py check_features_locked
```

## Front-end App

Set the environment variable
```
FRONTEND=True
```
This will set the front end app as the default app

## Style customization

Templates can now be overridden by placing the overrides in the `config/g3w-suite/overrides/templates`, a Docker service restart is required to make the changes effective.

The logo is also overridden (through `config/g3w-suite/settings_docker.py` which is mounted as a volume), changes to the settings file require the Docker service to be restarted.

A custom CSS is added to the pages, the file is located in `config/g3w-suite/overrides/static/style.css` and can be modified directly, changes are effective immediately.

## Performances optimization

General rules (in no particular order: they are all mandatory):

1. set scale-dependent visibility for the entire layer or for some filtered features (example: show only major roads until at scale 1:1E+6)
2. when using rule-based/categorized classification or scale-dependent visibility create indexes on the column(s) involved in the rule expression (example: "create index idx_elec_penwell_ious on elec_penwell_ious (owner);" )
3. start the project with only a few layers turned on by default
4. do not turn on by default base-layers XYZ such as (Google base maps)
5. do not use rule-based/categorized rendering on layers with too many categories (example: elec_penwell_public_power), they are unreadable anyway
6. enable redering simplification for not-point layers, set it to `Distance` `1.2` and check `Enable provider simplification if available`

## PostgreSQL administration

PostgreSQL runs in a Docker container. From the Docker checkout, connect as the configured database user:

```bash
docker compose exec postgis sh -c 'psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "${POSTGRES_DBNAME%%,*}"'
```

### Database backups

With the standard stack running and GNU Make installed, run the stable Docker checkout's backup target from its root:

```bash
make db-backup ENV=prod ID=before-upgrade
```

The script attempts to dump `G3WSUITE_POSTGRES_DBNAME`, `data_production` and `data_testing` to `backup/<ID>/` under `WEBGIS_DOCKER_SHARED_VOLUME`. Check the output for errors and verify that each expected `.bck` file was created before relying on the backup.

These are database dumps, not a full installation backup. Also back up projects, file-based data, uploads, mounted configuration and any databases not covered by the script. Keep a copy off the server. The `db-restore` target replaces databases: test recovery on a separate installation before using it on live data.

## Portainer usage
Portainer (https://www.portainer.io) is a docker-based web application used to edit and manage Docker applications in a simple and intuitive way.

See [Add a new stack](https://docs.portainer.io/user/docker/stacks/add) for how to deploy the standard Compose file with Portainer.
